purpose: Render premise-first study material in a modal, multi-language, draggable workbench without implying execution capabilities that do not exist.

uiContract.sourceAuthority: StudySyndicate contracts and problem packets remain authority; UI only renders them.

facets.label: Understand
facets.goal: Restate premise, inputs, output, constraints, and example before implementation.

facets.label: Implement
facets.goal: Write a working attempt in the selected language.

facets.label: Test / Debug
facets.goal: Use executable evidence or smallest counterexample to repair behavior.

facets.label: Explain
facets.goal: Explain correctness, tradeoffs, and complexity in your own words.

facets.label: Documentation
facets.goal: Practice finding official syntax/API documentation without solution lookup.

executionBoundary.principle: Guest code failure is data, not a host-shell failure.
executionBoundary.hostResponsibility: Every runner adapter catches or receives guest failure at its boundary and converts it into one normalized ExecutionOutcome. The React shell stays mounted.
invariants: Never infer runner availability from a language being listed.
Every executable adapter has a finite timeout or host-controlled cancellation path.
Guest exceptions must not escape into the React event loop.
Runner crashes become host-error outcomes with a recovery action.
The browser shell must not use eval or new Function for learner code until a dedicated sandbox contract is approved.
Unsupported execution remains a valid UI state and must explain the external tool or adapter required.

runner.exceptionModel: Python exceptions are caught by the host checker and normalized.
Compiler diagnostics, Result errors, and panics must be normalized by the host adapter.
Database errors and transaction failures must be normalized without crashing the shell.
Compiler failures, nonzero exit codes, signals, and timeouts must be normalized.
Thrown values, rejected promises, and timeouts must be contained by the sandbox adapter.
Type diagnostics and runtime failures must be normalized by the adapter.
Compiler errors, thrown exceptions, nonzero exit codes, and timeouts must be normalized.
Lua raises an error; the embedding host catches it and converts it to runtime-error without terminating the study shell.

panelLayout.rule: Drag-and-drop changes presentation order only; it never changes source authority, study mode, or runner capability.

acceptanceContract.statement: A learner can choose study target, facet, language, and study mode in one modal without editing code or config files.
The premise and source context are visible before the editable work area.
Python, Rust, SQL, C, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, and Lua have explicit runner kinds and availability; no language is treated as executable by assumption.
Guest failures normalize to ExecutionOutcome and cannot be allowed to crash the React host shell.
Premise, workspace, and feedback panels are reorderable with drag-and-drop while preserving semantic roles.
The editor remains a plain text/Notepad-like fallback when richer language services are unavailable.
Catalog-only exercises use neutral starters until their own premise-first packet defines an exercise-specific scaffold.
The root Vite/React/TypeScript application builds and lints in CI.
